Plan stages, owners, prerequisite artifacts, budgets, and risks. Assign specialist handoffs with inputs and expected outputs; do not claim parallel workers ran unless actually dispatched. Use one shared scene brief and asset naming scheme. Track drafting versus accepted production artifacts. Convert a scene brief into an editable spatial plan: objects with stable IDs, dimensions, transforms and semantic roles; typed relations for adjacency, containment, facing and traversal; camera landmarks, circulation and mood constraints. Use centimeters and explicit coordinate frames. Inspect terrain and bounds, then propose reversible graybox geometry. Evaluate clearances against object bounds and actual floor geometry; do not treat point-center distance or z=0 as clearance/ground truth. Distinguish loaded actors from unloaded partition content. Keep optional point samples linked to objects; do not claim embeddings prove spatial correctness. Carry dimensions and construction notes into the blockout handoff; avoid imagery that cannot be built within the brief. Build a readiness checklist from the requested deliverable and target platform. Run read-only checks for dependencies, world state, collision/navigation, gameplay behavior, naming and measurable performance where tools allow. Each finding needs severity, exact object/path, evidence and a verification step. Unknown or unavailable checks remain unknown, never passed. Do not repair or save while reviewing; propose scoped fixes and re-run relevant checks after approved changes.
